items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: Joe Wilder and I joined the band at the same time in San Francisco, Hamp's band. And they isolated us, and we were roommates on the road, two newest guys in the band.

ctx.x: Hear what I'm saying to you. I'm tell -- see, Joe Wilder and I joined the band at the same time in San Francisco, Hamp's band. And they isolated us, and we were roommates on the road, two newest guys in the band. Joe took Carl George's place. And I took Illinois' place, and the syndicate was for Illinois and Carl George because that was the Joe Newman was with this.

And give you a strange thing about Joe Newman, they all looking at Joe and, you know, they don't know. We were on our way back, going towards East, going towards Chicago, and we got into Denver. We played Denver a night. Joe had been there a long time and going to have some fun. So he told -- he said to Hamp, said, why don't you call 102, signifying. 102 was Trumpet Reveille that Milton Buckner did with 64ths in it and everything.
